text.p: Applied Materials Inc., the world's biggest supplier of equipment to semiconductor makers, said Thursday its quarterly profits plunged, sending shivers through Wall Street about the industry's performance.

Applied Materials said profits fell 53 percent to $73.1 million, or 40 cents a share, in the fourth quarter ended Oct. 27, from $155.4 million, or 84 cents a share, in the 1995 period. The latest results include a charge of $25.1 million, or 9 cents a share, to cover structuring costs.
Sales fell 12.4 percent to $861.0 million from $982.7 million.
The drop, though expected by analysts, shows chip makers are still reluctant to expand and equip new plants after a tough year.
The earnings performance sent a chill across the Silicon Valley and Wall Street.
"This might pressure the chip stocks tomorrow, specifically the commodity chip makers," said Phil Orlando of Value Line Asset Management.
Santa Clara, Calif.-based Applied Materials said the downturn in the semiconductor industry, which started in early summer, will not be over soon.

"Looking forward, we believe the industry downturn could extend through the early part of 1997, with the last half of 1997 still uncertain. We are cautiously optimistic that memory device prices and inventory levels are stabilising in our customers' business," Chairman James Morgan said in a statement.

One indication is the lower orders Applied received. It said new orders of $683.2 million in the quarter were 42.9 percent below orders in the year-ago period, and lagged the $931.3 million in its third quarter.
A year ago, the semiconductor equipment business was in one of the strongest booms in history.
"I'd take these results as pretty much in line with expectations," said PaineWebber Inc. analyst Gunnar Miller.
Wall Street analysts' average estimate for the quarter was 48 cents a share excluding special charges, according to First Call. Applied would have earned 49 cents without its charge.
